coord_notes.shape: The stored object is \(\theta_0+\bigcup_{|S|=k}\mathbb R^S\), a union of coordinate \(k\)-planes (a cone in the axes.json sense); the Hard-Concrete map \(\theta_0+z(\alpha)\odot w\) is its training-time relaxation.
coord_notes.base_point: Apex as in VIII.B: \(\theta_0\) is the one point shared by all strata, where the union is not a manifold. The relaxed map at \((z,w)=(\mathbf 1,0)\) has full \(S_1\), so 'apex' describes the L0-projected image, not the relaxation.
coord_notes.gauge: Each stratum \(w_S\mapsto\theta_0+\iota_Sw_S\) is injective; the gates are clamped at \(z=1\) near the init \(\alpha_0=5\), so the Hadamard torus \((cz,w/c)\) is inactive there.
coord_notes.covariance: Support structure in the standard basis; magnitude/L0 selection commutes with signed permutations and homotheties, not with rotations.
coord_notes.rebasing: The union of \(k\)-planes is closed under scaling and supports can be re-learned each cycle: \(R_\infty=\theta_0+\mathrm{span}=\Theta\) (Thm V.3(a)).

methods.categorical_reading: Diff pruning is the learned-support object: its image is the union of all fixed-mask images of size \(k\), so every fixed-mask method (FISH, LT-SFT, PaFi, SIFT, ...) is one stratum of it via an A2 arrow. Its vertex \(\theta_0\) is the only point common to all strata, which makes it a cone with apex rather than a linear method.

obstructions.reason: A \(k\)-sparse update has rank up to \(\min(k,m,n)\), so for \(k>r\) its maximum rank exceeds LoRA\(_r\)'s (conversely a generic rank-1 update is dense, O1).
The union of all \(k\)-planes is not contained in the single \(k\)-plane of one fixed mask.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: union of k-planes (Cone), apex at the vertex common to all strata (the relaxed gate map is regular, as the note says), gauge none per stratum, image exactly MonxMon-covariant, M1, span (= Theta); matches VIII.B. Both obstructions verified. No changes.

coord_notes.shape: \(W_0+M\odot\Delta W\) with \(M\) the global top-\(k\) diagonal-Fisher mask fixed before training: a coordinate subspace of dimension \(k\).
coord_notes.covariance: Mask in the standard frame; Fisher top-\(k\) selection commutes with signed permutations, not with rotations or non-uniform rescalings.
coord_notes.rebasing: Fixed mask: \(R_K=R_1\) (Thm V.3 cor. 2); recomputing the Fisher mask at the merged weight would gain.

methods.categorical_reading: FISH is a mask in the standard frame chosen by a data statistic: linear, regular and gauge-free, the frozen coordinate-block cell of the cotangent table in Exposé IV. By Prop IV.2 its masked-gradient training produces the same trajectory as training the forward linear method \(W_0+M\odot\Delta W\).

arrows.note: Freeze Diff pruning's gates at their clamped init value \(z=\mathbf 1\) and \(w\) at 0 off \(M\): FISH\((M)\) is the stratum \(M\) of the learned-support cone (within the L0 budget when \(|M|\le k\)).
With RoSA's sparse support equal to \(M\), FISH is the sparse summand of LoRA \(\oplus\) sparse, the LoRA part held at its base value.

obstructions.reason: A \(k\)-entry mask update can have rank up to \(\min(k,m,n)>r\).
Fisher-top supports and PaFi's data-free bottom-\(|W_0|\) supports are generically different planes, so neither image contains the other.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived Lin/regular/none/MonxMon (Fisher top-k is only signed-permutation x homothety equivariant; MonxMon is the nearest key)/M1/idempotent, matching VIII.B. A2 into relaxed Diff pruning (h(0)=(alpha0,0)) and A5 into RoSA (LoRA held at (0,A0)) checked. Obstructions verified. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Classified by Child-Tuning\(_D\): a fixed top-\(p_D\) Fisher gradient mask, which by Prop IV.2 (frozen coordinate compression) is the forward linear method \(W_0+M\odot\Delta W\). Child-Tuning\(_F\) (a fresh Bernoulli\((p_F)\) mask each step, rescaled by \(1/p_F\)) is instead a B-kind schedule: per-step Lin, reach \(\Theta\), merge n/a, rebasing schedule.
coord_notes.shape: Fixed mask for the D variant; if decoupled weight decay is applied to all parameters, coordinates outside \(M\) also shrink and the identity with the masked forward method fails (Prop IV.2 excludes AdamW with \(\lambda>0\)).
coord_notes.covariance: Empirical-Fisher top-\(p_D\) selection in the standard basis: signed-permutation equivariant; the F variant's i.i.d. mask is permutation-invariant in law.
coord_notes.rebasing: Idempotent for the fixed mask; Child-Tuning\(_F\) is itself a rebasing scheme reaching \(\Theta\).

methods.categorical_reading: Child-Tuning\(_D\) is FISH under another name: the same coordinate subspace selected by an empirical Fisher, isomorphic to FISH whenever the supports agree. Child-Tuning\(_F\) leaves the slice: resampling the mask every step makes it a rebasing scheme whose reach is all of \(\Theta\), a regulariser rather than a parameter-efficient object.

arrows.note: Isomorphism for a common support \(M\); Child-Tuning\(_D\) uses the empirical Fisher with gold labels and FISH samples \(y\sim p_\theta\), so the selected masks can differ.
The fixed mask is one stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: Concerns Child-Tuning\(_F\) only (the classified D variant has the conditional isomorphism above): fresh Bernoulli masks every step accumulate a dense update, so its reach is not inside any fixed \(k\)-plane.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived for Child-Tuning_D: Lin/regular/none/MonxMon/M1/idempotent. Conditional iso to FISH (A3, h=id) and A2 into Diff pruning checked. Change: the fish-mask O1 obstruction contradicted the arrow to the same target; its reason now says it concerns Child-Tuning_F only.

coord_notes.shape: Phase 2 trains on the fixed support \(\mu=\text{top-}K\,|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(0)}|\); the dense phase 1 only computes the mask.
coord_notes.covariance: Magnitudes of a dense fine-tuning diff: signed-permutation equivariant, not rotation equivariant.
coord_notes.merge: Each SFT is added into \(\theta_0\); the composition \(S_L\circ S_T\) is translation by \(\phi_T+\phi_L\), since additive methods commute with translations (Prop V.2(a)).

methods.categorical_reading: LT-SFT is a fixed-mask linear method whose mask is read off a dense fine-tuning run (a lottery-ticket support). Because translations commute, language and task SFTs compose by \(\oplus\), the sum of two coordinate subspaces, with interference confined to the overlap of their supports.

arrows.note: The lottery-ticket support is one stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: Sparse updates on a 0.25-8\% support have rank far above \(r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: fixed lottery-ticket support in phase 2, Lin/regular/none/MonxMon/M1/idempotent; translation composition (Prop V.2(a)) correct. A2 arrow and O2 obstruction verified. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Classified by SPT-LoRA; SPT-Adapter puts bottleneck adapters on the sensitive matrices (E, Fun, neutral, M\(\infty\)).
coord_notes.shape: Per weight box either a fixed squared-gradient mask (Lin) or LoRA (determinantal cone): the product is a cone with vertex \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.base_point: Apex from the LoRA boxes (deficit \(r(n-r)\) each at \(B=0\)); the masked boxes are regular.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) on each LoRA box; none on masked boxes.
coord_notes.covariance: Sensitivity scores, the per-box switch and the masks are coordinatewise, so the whole method is only Mon\(\times\)Mon-covariant, although each LoRA box alone is \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.rebasing: LoRA boxes reach full matrices, masked boxes are idempotent: \(R_\infty=\theta_0+\mathrm{span}\) of the product cone.

methods.categorical_reading: SPT is a direct sum over weight boxes of FISH-type masks and LoRA cones, the choice per box being made by counting squared-gradient-sensitive entries. It is an \(\oplus\)-word in \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\), so its expressivity is the product of its summands' images.

arrows.note: RoSA on all of SPT's boxes with SPT's masks as its sparse support: freeze RoSA's LoRA at its base value on the boxes where SPT uses masks.

obstructions.reason: On masked boxes the sparse update can have rank above \(r\).
The LoRA boxes give dense low-rank updates outside any fixed coordinate plane.

methods.check_notes: Jacobian check (one LoRA box 8x12, r=2, plus a 7-entry mask box): d = 43 = r(m+n-r)+k, dim S1 = 23, deficit 20 = r(n-r), so Cone/apex confirmed; GL_r gauge, MonxMon, span confirmed. A2 into RoSA checked (RoSA's sparse part frozen at 0 on the LoRA boxes). No changes.

coord_notes.shape: Fixed bottom-\(k\) \(|W_0|\) mask per matrix (data-free, shared by all tasks), plus every normalisation parameter (an LN-tuning summand).
coord_notes.covariance: The mask is a \(\theta_0\)-dependent function of \(|W_0|\): covariant under signed permutations and homotheties only, a subgroup of Mon\(\times\)Mon.
coord_notes.merge: Only existing entries and norm parameters change in place; the LN summand needs no fold.

methods.categorical_reading: PaFi is a fixed coordinate subspace chosen from the base point alone, plus an LN-tuning summand: a \(\theta_0\)-dependent mask with the opposite magnitude rule to LIFT. One mask shared by all tasks puts every PaFi adapter in the same linear space, so task-arithmetic combinations of them stay inside PaFi.

arrows.note: The bottom-\(k\) support (and LN coordinates) is one stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: Bottom-\(|W_0|\) and top-\(|\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0)|\) supports are generically different (and nearly disjoint, though not exactly), and LIFT never trains PaFi's normalisation parameters, so PaFi's plane is not inside LIFT's reach.
A data-free magnitude support and a Fisher support are generically different planes.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived Lin/regular/none/MonxMon/M1/idempotent (LN summand edits parameters in place). Change: lift obstruction reason corrected; the two supports are different but not generically disjoint (47 of 1310 entries overlap on a 512x512 Gaussian W0), and LIFT never trains LN parameters. O1 still holds.

coord_notes.shape: Union of \(l\times l\) tiles (\(l=256\)) selected after a short gradient warm-up and then fixed: a coordinate subspace of dimension \(m_Wl^2\).
coord_notes.covariance: Contiguous \(256\times256\) tiles impose a block partition the network does not have; a neuron permutation scatters a tile (\(\Pi_{\rm blocks}\), as for MoRA and GraLoRA).
coord_notes.rebasing: Fixed tiles: cycles gain nothing.

methods.categorical_reading: SMT is a block mask: the coordinate subspace of a few full tiles, GraLoRA's block partition without the low-rank factor. Each selected tile is full rank, which is why it does not plateau in rank as LoRA does.

arrows.note: The tile support is one fixed coordinate set, a stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: A selected tile has rank up to \(l=256>r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: fixed l x l tiles, Lin/regular/none/Pi (a neuron permutation scatters a tile)/M1/idempotent. A2 arrow and O2 obstruction verified. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: \(\theta'=\theta+\mathrm{scatter}(\eta,\phi)\) with a discrete index set \(\eta\) and real deltas \(\phi\): a reparametrisation whose \(Q\) is a disjoint union of coordinate planes.
coord_notes.shape: Dropped deltas leave the support (the weight reverts to \(\theta_0\) there), so the stored diff is \(d_\phi\)-sparse per tensor: a union of coordinate planes as for Diff pruning, with a per-tensor instead of a global budget.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\phi=0\) at \(\theta_0\), the vertex shared by all strata (apex in the sense used for Diff pruning).
coord_notes.rebasing: Drop-and-grow moves between strata without merging, so it is not a schedule; merge-and-restart with fresh supports reaches \(\Theta\).

methods.categorical_reading: SpIEL is a learned-support object like Diff pruning, but it searches the strata of the union of \(k\)-planes by drop-and-grow instead of a relaxed L0 gate. It is not a rebasing scheme, because dropped deltas are discarded rather than merged.

arrows.note: Componentwise on each support \(\eta\): every per-tensor stratum is a stratum of the global \(k\)-sparse union with \(k=\sum d_\phi\).

obstructions.reason: SpIEL's union of strata is not contained in LT-SFT's single fixed plane.
A \(d_\phi\)-sparse update can have rank above \(r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: dropped deltas revert to theta0, so the image is a union of d_phi-sparse planes as for Diff pruning (R, Cone, apex in the same sense, none, MonxMon, M1, span). A2 arrow (componentwise freezing on each support, pointed) and both obstructions verified. No changes.

coord_notes.shape: Exactly \(K\) entries per row (output neuron), chosen by \(|\nabla\mathcal L_{SCL}|\) before training and then fixed.
coord_notes.covariance: A row-regular support is preserved by row and column permutations; selection by gradient magnitude is signed-permutation equivariant, not rotation equivariant.

methods.categorical_reading: GPS is a fixed mask with a row-regular support of \(K\) incoming connections per neuron. Row regularity constrains which stratum of the \(k\)-sparse union is chosen, not the shape of the object.

arrows.note: The row-balanced support is one stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: For a dataset-aggregated (generically high-rank) gradient the row-wise top-\(K\) columns vary across rows and the masked update has rank up to \(\min(m,n)>r\). (For a rank-one gradient every row would select the same \(K\) columns and the rank would be at most \(K\).)

methods.check_notes: Re-derived Lin/regular/none/MonxMon/M1/idempotent. Change: lora O2 reason qualified; numerically a rank-one gradient makes every row pick the same K columns (rank <= K), so the full-rank claim needs a dataset-aggregated gradient.

coord_notes.shape: \(\Delta W=VU_S^\top\) with \(U_S\) a frozen one-hot selector of \(s\) heads/channels: the matrices supported on \(s\) whole columns (input side of \(W_O\), \(W_{\rm down}\)).
coord_notes.covariance: \(GL\) on the dense (output) side, monomial on the selected side (hidden-unit permutations and scalings carry the selector): \(GL\times\)Mon in (output)\(\times\)(input) order, the one-sided key MonxGL.
coord_notes.rebasing: Fixed selector: idempotent. Co-permuting coupled matrices to make the channels contiguous is a function-preserving base change (a hidden-unit permutation, Def V.1(a)): it changes the memory layout, not the object.

methods.categorical_reading: S\(^2\)FT is LoRA-FA whose frozen factor is a coordinate selector, \(\Delta W=VU_S^\top\): the structured-sparse and the low-rank readings are one linear object. Its dense-compute trick is a base change by a hidden-unit permutation, a symmetry of \(f\), so it costs nothing in expressivity.

arrows.note: Isomorphism S\(^2\)FT \(\cong\) LoRA-FA\((A_0=U_S^\top)\) of rank \(|S|\); \(s\) is LoRA-FA's scale.
LoRA pointed at \((0,U_S^\top)\), the same stratum as the default pointing \((0,A_0)\) (Thm II.2).
The \(s\) selected columns form one fixed coordinate set.

obstructions.reason: Entrywise Fisher supports generically do not contain whole columns, and whole columns are not entrywise-selected.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: Delta W = V U_S^T injective (d = m s, Jacobian check), Lin/regular/none, GL (output) x Mon (input) = key MonxGL, M1, idempotent. LoRA-FA iso, A2 into LoRA at (0,U_S^T) and A2 into Diff pruning checked; FISH O1 verified. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Gradient hooks apply a frozen coordinate projection \(P_S\); with \(S\) fixed this is the forward linear method by Prop IV.2.
coord_notes.shape: Support = top-\(x\%\) of \(|g_1|\) from the first batch(es), then fixed.

methods.categorical_reading: SIFT is a fixed coordinate mask chosen by the magnitudes of the first gradient, implemented as a backward projection with a frozen coordinate compression. By the degree-one collapse it is the same object as training \(W_0+P_S(\Delta W)\) directly.

arrows.note: The first-gradient support is one stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: Top \(|g_1|\) on one batch and top \((\sum_{\rm burn\text{-}in}g)^2\) rank coordinates differently, so the two fixed planes differ.
Sparse updates can have rank above \(r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: frozen coordinate projection, Lin by Prop IV.2 (no decoupled decay), regular/none/MonxMon/M1/idempotent. Arrow and both obstructions verified. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: The forward map is the identity; at step \(t\) compression and anchor are the coordinate projection onto layer group \(G_{\pi(t\bmod k)}\), changed every step in a fixed cycle.
coord_notes.shape: Per step the linear space of the active group's weights; one cycle visits every group.
coord_notes.covariance: Each active box is fully trainable, so every stage image is \(GL\times GL\)-covariant box by box (as for surgical FT and BitFit); the layer grouping partitions the set of boxes, not the coordinates of any box, and no neuron permutation or residual rotation breaks it. LISA and BAdam carry the same value after consolidation; VIII.B still lists LISA under \(\Pi\) (blocks).
coord_notes.rebasing: A rebasing scheme with period 1 and a cyclic shape; \(R=\Theta\) after one cycle. Each group's optimizer state is offloaded and resumed, so no state is reused across different frames (unlike GaLore).

methods.categorical_reading: HiFT is block-coordinate descent over layer groups: a backward lens whose anchor is a coordinate projection rotated every step, the resampled-every-step coordinate-block cell of Exposé IV. Since each group keeps its own optimizer state, the schedule is full fine-tuning in a cyclic order and reaches \(\Theta\) after one cycle.

arrows.note: Per stage: stage \(j\) of HiFT is the forward linear method of surgical FT on the block \(G_j\).

obstructions.reason: A HiFT stage makes full-rank updates of every matrix in the active group; a GaLore period has rank \(\le r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived B/Lin/regular/none/na/schedule. Covariance kept GLxGL by the decision procedure (box-wise fully trainable stages). Change: covariance note rewritten to state the disagreement with LISA/BAdam (Pi) explicitly instead of pointing to a non-existent issues list. Per-stage A3 arrow to surgical FT and O2 obstruction verified. Consolidation (2026-10-01): covariance note updated: LISA and BAdam harmonised to GLxGL.

coord_notes.shape: One contiguous block of layers fully trainable: the coordinate subspace \(\Theta_{B_j}\).
coord_notes.covariance: Every selected box is fully trainable (Full FT on that box), so the image is \(GL\times GL\)-covariant box by box.
coord_notes.rebasing: Fixed block. Auto-RGN instead trains all tensors with per-tensor learning rates \(\propto\) RGN: Full FT's image with a block-scalar metric \(\Lambda\), not a different object.

methods.categorical_reading: Surgical FT is a fixed coordinate block of whole layers: Full FT on the chosen block and frozen elsewhere, the shift type deciding which block. Auto-RGN keeps Full FT's image and changes only the metric \(\Lambda\) through per-tensor learning rates (Exposé III).

arrows.note: The block's coordinates form one fixed support; inside the \(k\)-sparse union only when \(|\Theta_{B_j}|\le k\).
When \(B_j\) is a HiFT group, the one-stage scheme embeds as stage \(j\) of HiFT's cycle, the other stages padded with their base value.

obstructions.reason: Full-rank updates on every matrix of the block exceed rank \(r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived R/Lin/regular/none/GLxGL/M1/idempotent (Full FT on one block, like BitFit). A2 into Diff pruning (conditional on budget) and A5 one-stage embedding into HiFT checked. No changes.

coord_notes.shape: \(\rho(m)=W_0\odot\mathbb 1[m\ge\tau]\): the orbit of \(\theta_0\) under the Boolean monoid \(\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) acting by Hadamard product, a finite set (\(d=0\)) that keeps the zeros of \(W_0\). The straight-through surrogate treats it as the Hadamard torus closure \(W_0\odot S\) (Lin).
coord_notes.base_point: Scores are initialised so that about 5\% of weights start masked: \(e=-(\mathbf 1-M_0)\odot W_0\ne0\) by design.
coord_notes.gauge: \(\rho\) depends only on the sign pattern of \(m-\tau\); the generic fibre is an open orthant cell, exactly an orbit of the positive torus \(\mathbb R_{>0}^{mn}\) acting by \(m\mapsto\tau+c\odot(m-\tau)\) (fibre dim \(mn\)). The scores move only through the STE surrogate.
coord_notes.covariance: Hadamard masking commutes with monomial changes of basis (diagonals commute, permutations permute the mask), not with rotations.
coord_notes.merge: \(W_0\odot M\) is an ordinary matrix of the original shape.
coord_notes.rebasing: \((W_0\odot M_1)\odot M_2=W_0\odot(M_1M_2)\): the Boolean monoid is idempotent, \(S^K=S\).

methods.categorical_reading: Masking is a monoid-orbit method: the Boolean monoid acts on \(\theta_0\) by Hadamard product, so the image is the finite vertex set of the box between \(0\) and \(W_0\), which keeps \(W_0\)'s zeros and can only create new ones. Its real-valued scores are pure torus gauge of the exact \(\rho\), and the 5\% masked start makes it an object with a pointing defect.

obstructions.reason: Same unpointed object \(M\mapsto W_0\odot M\), but Masking is pointed at \(W_0\odot M_0\ne\theta_0\) and Piggyback at \(\theta_0\): no pointed arrow either way.
Pointing defect: \(\rho(q_0)=W_0\odot M_0\ne\theta_0\), although every image point with at most \(k\) zeroed entries lies in Diff pruning's union.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: Boolean Hadamard monoid orbit (finite image, d=0), defect from the 5% masked start, positive-torus gauge on the orthant cells (fibre dim mn), exact MonxMon, M1, idempotent. Both O3 obstructions verified (no pointed arrow when rho(q0) != theta0). No changes.

coord_notes.shape: Orbit of \(\theta_0\) under the Boolean Hadamard monoid \(\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\); a finite image (\(d=0\)).
coord_notes.base_point: \(m^r_0=10^{-2}>\tau=5\cdot10^{-3}\): the mask starts all ones, \(\rho(q_0)=\theta_0\); with \(d=0\), \(\dim S_1=0=d\), regular trivially.
coord_notes.gauge: Real-valued mask weights matter only through \(\mathbb 1[m^r\ge\tau]\): positive torus acting about the threshold, fibre dim \(mn\); trained by the STE surrogate.
coord_notes.covariance: Hadamard structure in the standard basis on both sides.
coord_notes.rebasing: The Boolean monoid is idempotent: cycles only zero more entries.

methods.categorical_reading: Piggyback is the orbit of \(\theta_0\) under the Boolean Hadamard monoid, pointed at its identity \(\mathbf 1\): the earliest selective method is an action method, not an additive one. Its update \(-(\mathbf 1-M)\odot W_0\) is a sparse diff forced to equal \(-W_0\) on its support, which is the precise sense in which it is dual to Diff pruning.

arrows.note: \(Q\) read as the discrete set of binary masks; defined on masks zeroing at most \(k\) entries (all masks for the unbudgeted relaxation), pointed since \(h(\mathbf 1)=(\alpha_0,0)\).

HiRA \(W_0\odot(\mathbf 1+BA)\) with inner rank \(r=n\), pointed at \((0,I_n)\) (for \(r=n\) every \(B_0=0\), full-rank-\(A_0\) pointing is isomorphic to this one); both keep the zeros of \(W_0\). For \(r<\min(m,n)\) and \(W_0\) without zeros there is no arrow (O1): \(W_0\odot M\in\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HiRA}_r\) needs \(\operatorname{rank}(M-\mathbf 1)\le r\), which a generic binary mask violates.

obstructions.reason: Same unpointed object, different pointings (\(\mathbf 1\) versus a 5\%-masked \(M_0\)).
\(-(\mathbf 1-M)\odot W_0\) can have rank up to \(\min(m,n)>r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived Orb/regular (d=0, S1=0)/torus/MonxMon/M1/idempotent. Arrows checked numerically: rho_DP(alpha0, -(1-M).W0) = W0.M and rho_HiRA(M-1, I_n) = W0.M exactly, both pointed. Change: the HiRA arrow note called the r<min(m,n) failure O2; it is an image obstruction (O1), since rank(M-1) is not a cut-rank of Delta W.

coord_notes.shape: \(\theta_0+M\Delta\theta\) with \(M\) a fixed diagonal 0/1 matrix: the minimiser of the second-order surrogate under \(H\preceq|\lambda_{\max}|I\), i.e. the top-\(\lfloor mp\rfloor\) squared accumulated burn-in gradient.
coord_notes.covariance: Coordinatewise score in the standard basis: signed-permutation equivariant.

methods.categorical_reading: SAM picks one stratum of the \(k\)-sparse union by a second-order criterion and trains that fixed coordinate subspace. Its claim that every PEFT method is \(\theta_0+M\Delta\theta\) holds for linear methods up to a transport \(T\) (Prop II.13), but not for cones such as LoRA, whose image is a union of planes rather than one plane.

arrows.note: The SAM support is one stratum of the learned-support cone.

obstructions.reason: SAM ranks by \((\sum_t g_t)^2\) and FISH by \(\sum_n g_n^2\): different supports, so different planes.
Sparse updates can have rank above \(r\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived Lin/regular/none/MonxMon/M1/idempotent. Arrow and both obstructions verified; the remark that the theta0+M Delta theta claim fails for cones is correct. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: The forward map is the identity; the masked update \(W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta M_t\odot\hat g_t\) writes into \(W\), and \(M_t\) (top-\(k\) entries of \(\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_t)\)) is recomputed from the current weight every interval: a coordinate-mask lens re-pointed from the merged weight.
coord_notes.shape: Per interval the coordinate subspace of the current mask; the accumulated \(\Delta W\) lies on the union of the masks visited.
coord_notes.covariance: \(\mathrm{SVD}_r\) is \(CO\times CO\)-equivariant and top-\(k\) magnitude only signed-permutation equivariant; the composite rule keeps their intersection (signed permutations times homotheties), inside Mon\(\times\)Mon.
coord_notes.rebasing: Masks recomputed from the merged weight gain (Thm V.3 cor. 2): a schedule whose reach grows with the union of masks.

methods.categorical_reading: LIFT is a LISA-type rebasing scheme in the coordinate frame: each interval trains a fixed mask, and the next mask is read from the principal part of the merged weight, so its anchor depends on \(\theta\) across intervals. The spectral filter changes which coordinates are chosen, not the coordinate geometry of the image.

arrows.note: First interval only (mask \(M_0\) from \(\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0)\)); later intervals are the same kind of object re-based at \(W_t\).

obstructions.reason: Top entries of \(\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0)\) and bottom entries of \(|W_0|\) are generically different supports (nearly, not exactly, disjoint), so LIFT's first-interval plane is not inside PaFi's plane.

Conditional: once LIFT's masks change across intervals, its accumulated \(\Delta W\) is supported on the union of the masks visited; when that union exceeds SpIEL's per-tensor budget \(d_\phi\), \(d(\mathrm{LIFT})>d(\mathrm{SpIEL})\). A single LIFT interval with \(k\le d_\phi\) is a stratum of SpIEL's union, so the obstruction is to the schedule, not to one stage.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived B/Lin/regular/none/MonxMon (nearest key)/na/schedule. A2 first-interval arrow checked. Changes: pafi O1 reason (supports different, not disjoint); spiel O2 reason made explicitly conditional (holds for the schedule once the union of masks exceeds d_phi, not for one interval).

coord_notes.shape: \(\Delta W=sBAP\) with \(P=I_{n/g}\otimes\mathbf 1_g^\top\) the group-sum pooling: LoRA\(_r\) on the pooled space composed with \(Y\mapsto YP\), image \(\kappa\theta_0+\{YP:\operatorname{rk}Y\le r\}\), \(d=r(m+n/g-r)\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(q_0=(0,A_0)\): \(\rho(q_0)=\kappa\theta_0\), defect \(e=\kappa\theta_0-\theta_0\) as for QLoRA (apex relative to \(\kappa\theta_0\)).

This is the fine-tune-then-quantise order, which is why its merge stays exactly in the quantised type.
